x: The cerebellum keeps balance, posture and smooth coordination of muscles. The cerebrum handles thinking, the medulla vital reflexes and the hypothalamus temperature and hunger.
t: Recall the function of each brain part.

x: Option C is incorrect: brain tissue has no pain receptors, which is why brain surgery can be done on awake patients. The other statements are right.
t: Recall that the brain itself feels no pain.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the pons being part of the brainstem is structure, not the reason the brainstem controls vital functions.
t: Check whether R is a cause or only structure.

x: Sensory nerves carry signals from receptors to the CNS, motor nerves from the CNS to effectors, mixed nerves both, and the autonomic system controls involuntary functions, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the direction of each nerve type.

x: I, II and IV are correct: cranial nerves come from the brain, spinal nerves from the cord, and the somatic system controls voluntary muscle. III is false because the autonomic system is involuntary.
t: Discriminate somatic (voluntary) from autonomic (involuntary).

x: All six are correct: the cerebrum handles thinking, memory, reasoning, sensation, speech and learning.
t: Recall the functions of the cerebrum.

x: All six are medulla functions: it controls heartbeat and breathing and the reflexes of swallowing, vomiting, coughing and sneezing.
t: Recall the functions of the medulla.

x: All five are hypothalamus roles: body temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep and circadian rhythm.
t: Recall the functions of the hypothalamus.

x: The cerebellum (Latin for "little brain") sits below the cerebrum at the back of the skull.
t: Recall the other name of the cerebellum.

x: Heart rate is regulated by the cardiac centre in the medulla through the autonomic nerves. The cerebellum handles balance.
t: Recall where vital centres are located.

x: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves from the brain and 31 pairs of spinal nerves from the spinal cord, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall 12 cranial and 31 spinal pairs.

x: A reflex arc runs through the spinal cord, bypassing the brain, so it gives a rapid involuntary response such as pulling a hand from heat.
t: Recall the nature of a reflex.

x: The adult skeleton has 206 bones; a newborn has about 300, which fuse as it grows.
t: Recall the bone count of an adult.

x: Option B is incorrect: the radius is on the thumb side of the forearm; the ulna is on the little-finger side. The femur, patella and stapes facts are right.
t: Discriminate radius (thumb side) from ulna.

x: Both are true and R explains A: red marrow inside bones makes blood cells, which is how the skeleton contributes to their formation.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The humerus is the upper arm, the atlas holds the skull, the sternum anchors the rib cage and the axis lets the head turn, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the role of each bone.

x: I, II and III are correct: there are 7 cervical, 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae. IV is false because the floating ribs are 11 and 12.
t: Recall the counts of vertebrae and ribs.

x: The tibia is the main weight-bearing shin bone, the fibula the thin outer leg bone, the sternum supports the rib cage and the atlas (C1) holds the skull, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the location and role of each bone.

x: The axis (C2) allows neck rotation, the ribs protect heart and lungs, the skull protects the brain and the vertebral column protects the spinal cord, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the location and role of each bone.

x: All three are correct: there are 12 pairs of ribs; ribs 1–7 are true ribs joined directly to the sternum, and ribs 11–12 are floating ribs with no front attachment.
t: Recall the classification of ribs.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The human body has 12 pairs of ribs.
II. True ribs are ribs 1–7.
III. Ribs 11 and 12 are called floating ribs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

x: All five are correct: the skeleton supports, moves with muscles, protects, stores calcium and phosphorus, and yellow marrow stores fat.
t: Recall the functions of the skeleton.
